Composition: cluster shares, subtype shifts and composition-driven DE

Source: R/assessComposition.R
assessComposition.Rd

A broad cluster can hold subtypes whose shares shift between the groups. Pseudobulk DE on the broad cluster then reports the subtypes' marker genes as differentially expressed although no gene changes within any subtype. This step measures that risk for every comparison, in four parts:

Usage

assessComposition(
  x,
  variance,
  sensitivity,
  power = 0.8,
  fdr = 0.05,
  reference = c("reference", "pooled"),
  thresholds = defaultThresholds()
)

Arguments

x

A S4Vectors::SimpleList from pbSetup().

variance

The list returned by estimateVariance().

sensitivity

The table returned by estimateSensitivity() (its per-gene alpha sets the MDE).

power

Target power for the MDE. Default 0.8.

fdr

FDR at which parent and child genes count as DE for the attribution. Default 0.05.

reference

Where the per-cell child expression c_gk comes from: "reference" (the contrast's reference group A only; default, which avoids attributing real within-child DE in B to composition) or "pooled" (all samples of the contrast's groups).

thresholds

A list from defaultThresholds(); uses compExplained.

Value

A list with summary (a data.frame, one row per comparison: the cluster share share_A, share_B, share_fdr; the composition status; the most shifted child comp_child with comp_share_A, comp_share_B and comp_min_fdr; exp_comp_deg, frac_comp_expected; n_comp_sensitive, frac_comp_sensitive; n_parent_deg, n_comp_driven, frac_comp_driven), genes (per gene and comparison: lfc_comp, comp_power, mde, sensitive, the observed logfc, padj, parent_de, child_de and the attribution label) and proportions (per sample and child, the child's share of the parent).

Details

  1. Cluster share (every annotation level, reported only): the cluster's share of each sample's cells, A vs B, tested with speckle::propeller (arcsin-square-root proportions, limma). A cluster whose share shifts is not a problem for DE within it, so this never changes the call.

  2. Subtype shift within the cluster (needs a finer annotation nested in this one, see pbSetup()): propeller on the children's shares of the parent's cells, over the comparison's samples.

  3. Composition-sensitive genes (prospective): per gene, the log2 fold change the observed subtype shift alone would produce in the parent's library-size-normalised pseudobulk, log2[(sum_k pB_k c_gk / sum_k pB_k L_k) / (sum_k pA_k c_gk / sum_k pA_k L_k)], with p the donor-averaged child shares, c_gk the per-cell mean count of gene g in child k and L_k the child's per-cell library size. Each gene's power to be called DE at that shift-only change (layer 4, at the comparison's per-gene alpha) is comp_power; their sum, exp_comp_deg, is the number of DEGs the shift alone is expected to produce, and frac_comp_expected its share of the testable genes. callComparisons() flags the comparison Caution when a child's shift is significant and frac_comp_expected reaches thresholds$compFrac. Genes whose shift-only change exceeds their own MDE (sensitive, counted in n_comp_sensitive) are reported too, but many genes each at modest power add up to many artefacts without any of them clearing the MDE, so that count understates the risk (E6).

  4. Attribution of the observed parent DEGs (retrospective, reported only): each gene the method's own test calls DE in the parent at fdr is labelled composition-driven (DE in no child comparison, and the shift-only change has the same sign and explains at least thresholds$compExplained of the observed change), within-child DE (DE in at least one child), mixed (both) or unresolved (neither, or no child comparison could be fitted).

Clusters without a finer annotation nested in them get composition = "not assessed"; parts 2-4 need two annotation levels.
